title: Possible {name} in source
description: The file contains {name}. The URL carries a user name and password in its authority section, so every reader, log line and backup that touches the file inherits the account. Shape-only: the match does not prove the endpoint is reachable.
remediation: Rotate the account in the connection string, then supply the URL from the environment or a secret manager so the password never lands in the repository.
limitation: Shape-only: a URL-shaped literal with a user:password authority carrying 6+ password characters. It cannot prove the endpoint is reachable or the account is live.
fp: Placeholder URLs such as postgres://user:password@localhost in documentation and compose samples are the common false positives; the rule requires 6+ password characters and vetoes EXAMPLE text.
recordDesc: {name} embeds datastore or broker credentials in a URL. Every reader, log shipper and backup that touches the file inherits the account, so rotation plus environment injection is the only durable fix.
applicability: Source, .env files, compose files and CI configuration that may embed {name}.
risk: Authenticated access to the datastore or broker behind the URL; HIGH severity.
why: {name} with an inline password hands the account to everyone who can read the file, and the password does not rotate itself.
fix: Rotate the account used by the connection string.
Move the URL into the environment or a secret manager and reference it by name.
Check logs and backups for the same URL and purge them.
verifyT: The old password no longer authenticates and no URL with an inline password remains at this name.
